newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bids $64-$65, passed-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bids $64-$65, passed-feedlots.

text.p: Fed cattle top bids near midday Tuesday were raised $1.00 to $65.00 per cwt in the Texas Panhandle area, matching light sales on Monday and heavy trade last week, but owners passed and continued to ask $66.00 to $67.00, with a few asking $68.00, feedlot sources said.
"I think we'll trade at $66.00 on Wednesday, but right now they (owners) seem content to sit back and wait," one Texas Panhandle feedlot operator said.
Bids in Kansas remained at $64.00, with owners there also passing the bids and asking $66.00 to $67.00, several Kansas cattle feeders said.
Fed cattle prices were seen underpinned by light supplies of market-ready cattle compared with last week, feedlot sources said.
Active sales last week depleted most showlists by Wednesday, including a large number of cattle carried over from the previous week.
Outlooks for continued strength in beef prices also were seen buoying fed cattle prices this week, they said.
Beef cut-out prices at midday Tuesday were quoted up $0.70 to $1.12 per cwt, with 154 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported.
